ratings_why.fun: Over a 7 because a Guise brings its tribe, so every lobby makes new combos: a Kit in a Bird's Guise flies south, Pip mirrors Pass into a second lane, the Lady stacks Belly, Mire and Pass on one body.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7 because no tribe trades with the shop or reads the enemy's text; Exchange (freeze as an eighth slot, buy back to replay When played) and Penny's steal-and-silence are new verbs.

verdict_why: One real loop to close (Coat-Peg Steward copying stats on each round-trip Exchange) and one unclear line in Exchange; the rest should stay as it is.

points.text: Coat-Peg Steward copies the given unit's gains while that unit keeps them in the shop. Exchange the new unit back for it and it comes home with 2X+2, so each Exchange doubles. Make the Steward move the stats (the given unit loses them).
Exchange ends with "and a token is removed", which a player can't read. Say which token, or cut the clause.
Matron of the Exchange Room buffs a random unit per tribe. Buffing the Changeling that brings each tribe would make Guise choice steer the growth.
Wicker Moll plus Counter Stand-In turns one sale into two copies of the sold text; that is the best hidden combo here, and a build line could name it.

standouts.why: Pip Unlike's mirror turns one-sided texts like Pass into a new lane; a small card with many off-label uses.
Penny Second steals the enemy's key text and silences it, and the visible next board makes her placement a real decision.
The Lady Under the Hill pays off every Guise you chose all game in one body.

weakest.why: Veil-Stitcher is a plain team buffer with a Guise check; no decision beyond wearing one.
Bettie Underhill just counts Exchanges; the payoff is a number, not a new interaction.
Long-Stay Hollin is a straight keep-your-Guise buffer; the keep-or-swap choice is already carried by the Hob.

flags.note: Round-trip Exchanges with Placement Officer or Midnight Swap double a unit's gained stats each time.
Keeper of the Lost Hour with the Lady doubles every stolen fight trigger on one body; fine in a fight, worth the owner's eye with goldens.
Weeks-Old Hob beside another Changeling copies its own text only, not its Guise; players may expect the Guise.
